review.raw_markdown: ## Skechers — "Did you forget something?" | Abandoned Cart Email --- ### 1. Executive Summary A competent but diluted abandoned cart email. The intent is clear — recover an incomplete checkout — but Skechers buries the urgency under layers of secondary content: a promotional banner, a plain-text category nav, and a utility block that collectively shift focus away from closing the cart. The hero does its job, but the email loses discipline fast. --- ### 2. Business Impact Score: **5 / 10** Functional recovery email with a solid promotional hook, but structural clutter and weak content below the fold reduce conversion potential. --- ### 3. What's Working - **Hero clarity.** "Ready to Check Out? Complete Your Order" is unambiguous. The product (Slip-ins Max Cushioning Arch Fit 2.0 – Terrain) is featured immediately above the fold with a direct CTA button. - **Promotional incentive is present.** The "Buy One Get 50%" mid-email banner adds a tangible purchase driver — a reason to act now that pure urgency alone can't provide. - **Top Sellers grid.** A horizontal row of additional shoe options creates light product discovery without derailing the primary goal. - **Utility footer is complete.** App download, curbside pickup, BNPL (Afterpay visible), and store finder are all present — covers the customer wherever they want to complete the transaction. --- ### 4. What's Weak - **The 50% offer is buried.** A meaningful promotional hook — Buy One Get 50% — appears well below the hero instead of alongside the CTA. If this offer applies to the abandoned cart, leading with it could meaningfully lift conversion. - **"Shop Additional Styles" is text-only.** The Women / Men / Kids / Clothing / New Arrivals / Sale category block has no images, no color, no visual hierarchy. It reads like a site map dropped into the middle of an email and contributes nothing. - **Email is too long for its purpose.** Abandoned cart emails should be tight. This one extends into a full browse/promotional email format, diluting the recovery message with category navigation, utility modules, and social links. - **Product details are small and hard to read.** The abandoned product name and price appear in small type below the product image — easily missed at a glance. - **The decorative frame around the hero looks dated.** The hand-drawn doodle border aesthetic doesn't match the premium athletic positioning Skechers is reaching for. --- ### 5. Recommendations 1. **Move the promotional incentive into the hero block** — surface "Buy One Get 50%" next to or directly below the "Complete Your Order" CTA so the offer lands before the customer scrolls. 2. **Cut or compress everything below the Top Sellers grid** — the category nav and utility block are appropriate for a newsletter, not a cart recovery email. Trim or move to a single footer line. 3. **Increase product name and price legibility** — use larger type or a callout treatment for the abandoned item's title and price to anchor the customer's memory of what they left behind. 4. **Modernize the hero visual treatment** — replace the doodle frame with a cleaner, bolder typographic layout consistent with current athletic brand standards. 5. **Add urgency language** — "Your cart expires soon" or stock scarcity signals give the email a second reason to act beyond the offer alone. --- ### 6. Bottom Line This email does the minimum required of an abandoned cart touchpoint but doesn't push to be a strong converter. The promotional hook is its most valuable asset and it's wasted mid-scroll. Tighten the structure, move the offer up, and cut the category clutter — this should be a 3-module email, not a 9-module one. --- ### 7. Evidence | Module | Observation | |---|---| | **Overall purpose** | Abandoned cart recovery — user left an item in checkout | | **Hero / primary value prop** | "Ready to Check Out? Complete Your Order" — clear call back to incomplete cart with CTA button; product image prominently featured | | **Membership / benefits** | None visible | | **Product discoverability** | Top Sellers horizontal grid provides secondary discovery; adequate but not rich | | **Utility / secondary modules** | Shop Additional Styles (text-only category list), App download, Curbside Pickup, Shop Now Pay Later (Afterpay), Find a Store — full suite but over-engineered for this email type | | **Bugs / friction / clarity issues** | No broken images or overlapping text visible; abandoned product text reads small; the hand-drawn hero frame feels visually inconsistent with the rest of the design | --- ## Technical Audit ## Technical Audit — Skechers "Did you forget something?" (Abandoned Cart) **Sender:** hello@msgs.skechers.com | **Platform:** Attentive Mail --- ### 1. Technical Summary Standard abandoned-cart email built on Attentive's platform using a table-based layout with responsive media queries. No structural build failures detected, but several tracking, accessibility, and compliance items require attention. --- ### 2. Link & Tracking Issues **HTTP redirect domain** — All click-tracking links use `http://` (not `https://`) at the Attentive redirect layer: ``` http://skechers.attentivemail.com/ls/click?upn=... ``` If the destination resolves to HTTPS, this causes an HTTP→HTTPS chain with a mixed-content hop. Verify the sending domain is enforcing HTTPS at the redirect layer. **UTM parameters unverifiable** — Destination URLs are fully encoded inside the Attentive `upn=` blob. It is not possible to confirm UTM params (source, medium, campaign) are appended post-redirect from the HTML source alone. QA must decode or test-click each link to verify UTM passthrough. **Web version link** — Present and tracked (`row-1 .column-2 a`). Functional, but label is lowercase `"web version"` — minor but inconsistent with brand copy conventions. --- ### 3. Rendering & Accessibility **Empty `` tag:** ```html <title> ``` Screen readers and some email clients (notably Outlook on Windows) surface the `` as the document label. Should be set to the subject line or campaign name. **Image `alt` attributes** — HTML is truncated before image blocks render; alt text could not be confirmed. QA must verify all `<img>` tags carry descriptive `alt` values, especially product/hero images which carry the cart content in abandoned-cart flows. **`text-size-adjust:none` on body** — Present as `-webkit-text-size-adjust:none; text-size-adjust:none`. This prevents iOS Mail from auto-scaling small text, which is intentional for layout control but will suppress font scaling for low-vision users on mobile. **Responsive breakpoint** — Media query fires at `max-width:620px`. Container is `width:600px`. This leaves a 20px gap where the responsive rules do not apply on viewports between 601–620px. Low-risk but worth noting. **`#MessageViewBody a { color:inherit; text-decoration:none }`** — Disables default link underlines inside Gmail. Acceptable if CTAs use button styling, but any inline text links will be visually indistinct from body copy. --- ### 4. Personalization & Merge Tokens **No first-name merge token visible** — Subject line ("Did you forget something?") and preheader ("You left something in your cart…") contain no first-name personalization despite this being a triggered, identified-user flow. Attentive supports `{{ first_name }}` tokens; their absence is a missed personalization opportunity and also a signal to check whether the template is falling back to a no-name variant or if tokens were stripped. **Cart content tokens** — HTML is truncated; dynamic cart line items (product name, image, price, quantity) could not be confirmed. These are critical for an abandoned-cart email and must be validated in QA sends with seeded cart data, including edge cases: empty cart fallback, multi-item cart, out-of-stock item. --- ### 5. Compliance **Unsubscribe link** — Not visible in the truncated source. CAN-SPAM requires a functional opt-out mechanism in every commercial email. Must be confirmed present in the full HTML (typically in the footer). Attentive-managed sends normally inject this automatically, but should be verified. **Physical mailing address** — Not visible in truncated source. CAN-SPAM §7(d) requires a valid physical postal address. Confirm it appears in the footer. **Sender domain** — `msgs.skechers.com` is a subdomain used by Attentive. SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment should be verified at the DNS level for this subdomain; misalignment causes deliverability failures at major ISPs. **Preheader padding technique** — Uses a mix of Unicode zero-width non-joiners (U+200D, `­`) and Mongolian vowel separators (U+180E, `͏`) for whitespace inflation. This is a known technique but some spam filters flag heavy use of invisible Unicode characters. Monitor deliverability metrics. --- ### 6. Email-to-Site Continuity **UTM passthrough unconfirmed** — As noted in §2, UTM parameters cannot be read from the encoded tracking URLs. For an abandoned-cart flow, the minimum expected UTM tags are: - `utm_source=attentive` (or `skechers_email`) - `utm_medium=email` - `utm_campaign=abandoned_cart` - `utm_content=<variant_id>` Missing or malformed UTMs will cause sessions to be attributed to direct/none in analytics, masking email revenue. **Landing page alignment** — Logo and "web version" links both route through Attentive redirects. The web version destination should render the full email at a stable URL; verify it does not 404 or redirect to the homepage after a session expiry window. --- ### 7. Recommendations | Priority | Item | |---|---| | High | Confirm unsubscribe link and physical address are present in full HTML footer | | High | Decode/test-click all tracked URLs to verify HTTPS at destination and UTM param presence | | High | Validate cart-item merge tokens with seeded QA sends, including empty-cart and OOS edge cases | | Medium | Set `<title>` to subject line or campaign name for screen reader compatibility | | Medium | Verify SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment for `msgs.skechers.com` sending subdomain | | Medium | Audit all `<img>` alt attributes in the full HTML (not visible in truncated source) | | Low | Consider adding first-name personalization to subject or preheader given this is an identified-user trigger | | Low | Evaluate HTTP→HTTPS redirect chain at the Attentive tracking domain |
